answer: Require every agent to earn influence only through endorsements from peers outside its own cluster, and score identities by their graph conductance: a Sybil ring looks like a canyon — deep, narrow, and cut off from the honest region — while real agents build broad bridges across it. A fake identity costs real effort to wire into the wider network, like hauling timber uphill, and its endorsements stay trapped inside its own clique. When one fake is exposed, the penalty ripples outward, discounting the whole cluster's weight, so running many identities costs more influence than it buys.
